title: Reading Files
summary: Read files with cat, head and tail, count lines with wc and scroll with less.
intro:
Files are full of text: notes, poems, logs, code.
In this lesson you will read a whole file, peek at the top and the bottom, count lines, and scroll through a file.
Two files are waiting for you: poem.txt and numbers.txt.
outro: Now you can read any file! cat for short files, head and tail for a quick peek, wc to count, and less for long ones.

steps.instruction: Show the whole poem in poem.txt on the screen.
hints: The command cat prints a file on the screen.
steps.explain: cat prints the whole file at once. It is great for short files. For long files, the text scrolls away too fast to read.

steps.instruction: Show only the first 3 lines of numbers.txt.
hints: head shows the head (the top) of a file. The option -n says how many lines.
steps.explain: Without -n, head shows the first 10 lines. head is handy to peek into a big file without printing all of it.

steps.instruction: Now show only the last 2 lines of numbers.txt.
hints: The opposite of head is tail. It also understands -n.
steps.explain: tail shows the end of a file. It is perfect for log files, where the newest lines are at the bottom.

steps.instruction: How long is numbers.txt? Count its lines.
hints: wc means 'word count'. The option -l counts lines.
steps.explain: wc -l counts lines. Plain wc shows three numbers: lines, words and characters. Don't worry if you see extra spaces in front of the number; some computers add them.

steps.instruction: Open poem.txt in the viewer less. Scroll with the arrow keys, and press q to quit.
hints: less is a file viewer. Space shows the next page, q quits.
Type: less poem.txt   (then press q to come back)
steps.explain: less lets you scroll through long files. Inside less, type /word and Enter to search for a word. The man pages use the same viewer, so these keys work there too.
